newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-Gencor approves Mozambique aluminium smelter.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gencor approves Mozambique aluminium smelter.

text.p: South Africa's Gencor Ltd said on Tuesday it would invest in a new $1.1 billion aluminium smelter in Mozambique which could propel it into the ranks of the world's top four aluminium producers.
"We are delighted to be able to give the green light for the Mozal smelter," Gencor chairman Brian Gilbertson said.

The 245,000-tonne-a-year primary aluminium smelter will be erected near the Mozambican capital Maputo. The contruction is subject to Gencor and its equity partner, South Africa's state-owned Industrial Development Corporation (IDC), securing international equity investment of $250 million.
"Gencor will invest $125 million in the project subject to the securing of international equity investment from suitable partners by the end of 1997," Gencor said in a statement.
"The Gencor decision follows on the approval in-principle decision taken by South Africa's Industrial Development Corporation board to invest a like amount of $125 million."
The smelter will be operated by Gencor unit Alusaf Ltd, which will also assume responsibility for its construction, Alusaf managing director Rob Barbour said at a presentation.
He said Gencor was open to anybody interested in taking up an equity stake in the remaining $250 million equity finance.
"As far as potential partners are concerned, we are totally open for suggestions, to anybody who is interested.
"The most interested participants will probably come from people who need metal, who consume metal like Japan and Korea," Barbour said.

The remaining funds needed for the project would be raised through quasi-equity and loan finance. Barbour said the World Bank's International Finance Corporation will take up substantial interest in the loan finance portion.

He said the capital cost estimate of $1.125 billion included escalation but excluded finance charges. The project is scheduled to completed in 31 months with the first metal production during the year 2000.

"The Mozal project supports Gencor's strategy to build on its leading, low cost alumina and aluminium industries and on its unique competence in implementing projects in southern Africa," Barbour said.
Alusaf currently operates two aluminium smelters in South Africa. The new, highly-successful Hillside plant and older Bayside smelter in Richards Bay.
Gencor said after the proposed listing of its offshore Billiton subsidiary on the London Stock Exhange, the responsibility for the project would be taken over by Billiton.
Barbour said the Mozal smelter will be by far the largest private sector investment in Mozambique -- which was only now emerging form the effects of a 16-year civil war.
"Mozal will jump-start the Mozambican economy...," Barbour said, adding: "Here is a project that will be a world beater."
The smelter will be built to expand capacity to 490,000 tonnes and the first phase will see construction of one potline with 288 pots.

Mozal project director Ian Reid said the increased production from the Mozal smelter could push Gencor to the position of the fourth largest aluminium producer in the world from its current fifth place.

The smelter will need about 435 MW of electricity to operate and Gencor said the project was viable because of a long-term competitive power price offered by South Afican utility Eskom with EDM, the Mozambique Electricity Supply Authority.
Other aspects that increased viability was the granting of an industrial free zone status to the project by the Mozambican government.
Alumina feedstock will be sourced from Billiton refineries in Australia, Suriname or Brazil. Billiton already supplies alumina to the Bayside and Hillside smelters.
